text: The Polanyi Medal is a biennial award given by the Royal Society of Chemistry to recognize outstanding contributions to the field of gas kinetics. It is presented at the International Symposium on Gas Kinetics following a plenary lecture delivered by the recipient. The medal is named in honor of Michael Polanyi, the Hungarian-British polymath who lived from 1891 to 1976 and whose research played a key role in establishing gas kinetics and reaction dynamics. John Polanyi, Michael's son, was awarded the Polanyi Medal in 1988.
